case_fields.case_id: Permanent identifier for the case (for example SDI-00012).
case_fields.maker: Vehicle maker the case was collected under.
case_fields.first_reported: Date of the earliest report found (YYYY-MM-DD).
case_fields.last_reported: Date of the most recent report found.
case_fields.sort_date: Date used to order cases: the incident date when coded, otherwise first_reported.
case_fields.headline: A representative headline, in the publisher's words.
case_fields.source_summary: A publisher's own one-line summary of its report (not written by this project).
case_fields.n_sources: Number of reports attached to the case.
case_fields.auto_model: Vehicle model found by word matching in headlines (uncoded cases only rely on this).
case_fields.auto_location: Place name found by word matching in headlines.
case_fields.auto_tags: Word-match labels, each worded "mentioned in coverage".
case_fields.narrative: Short neutral account of what coverage reports, drafted by the machine coder.
case_fields.review_status: "machine-coded, not yet reviewed" until a person has checked the record.
case_fields.text_basis: Fullest text the coder could read for the case: full_text, summary or headline.
case_fields.unsupported_values_removed: How many values the coder proposed that were removed because their supporting quotation could not be found in the report.
case_fields.merged_ids: Retired case IDs whose reports were joined into this case because they described the same event (see `retired_ids.csv`). Blank for most cases.
case_fields.url: Address of the case's page on the website.

variables.name: incident_date
variables.label: Incident date
variables.desc: Date the incident happened, as stated in coverage: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM or YYYY when only that much is given. Work out relative dates ("Thursday night") from the report's publication date.

variables.name: incident_type
variables.label: Type of incident

values.collision: The vehicle struck, or was struck by, something or someone.
values.near_miss_or_erratic_driving: No collision reported: a near miss, swerving, running a signal, wrong-way travel or similar.
values.traffic_stop_or_violation: No collision reported: the coverage centres on a police stop, citation or arrest.
values.driver_asleep_or_absent: No collision reported: the person in the car was seen asleep, out of the driver's seat, or absent.
values.low_speed_or_parking_manoeuvre: Something that happened while parking, summoning or creeping at walking pace.
values.other: An identifiable incident that fits none of the above.

variables.desc: What kind of event the coverage describes.

variables.name: collision_with
variables.label: Collided with

values.emergency_or_police_vehicle: Police, fire, ambulance or tow vehicle.
values.fixed_object: Pole, tree, barrier, wall, building and the like.

variables.desc: What the vehicle collided with, if there was a collision.

variables.name: vehicle_make
variables.label: Vehicle make
variables.desc: Make of the vehicle whose automated-driving feature is in question (for example Tesla).

variables.name: vehicle_model
variables.label: Vehicle model
variables.desc: Model, as named in coverage (for example Model Y, Cybertruck, Cybercab).

variables.name: vehicle_model_year
variables.label: Model year
variables.desc: Model year of that vehicle, when coverage gives it.

variables.name: location_city
variables.label: City or locality
variables.desc: City, town or county where the incident happened.

variables.name: location_state_region
variables.label: State or region
variables.desc: State, province or region, written in full.

variables.name: location_country
variables.label: Country
variables.desc: Country, written in full (for example United States).

variables.name: road_type
variables.label: Road setting

values.highway_or_freeway: Interstate, freeway, motorway or other limited-access road.

variables.desc: Where on the road network the incident happened.

variables.name: time_of_day
variables.label: Time of day
variables.desc: When in the day the incident happened.

variables.name: system_named
variables.label: Automated-driving feature named

values.full_self_driving: Tesla Full Self-Driving (FSD), supervised or otherwise.
values.robotaxi_or_driverless_service: A robotaxi or other vehicle operating with no driver.
values.unspecified: "Self-driving mode", "driver assistance" and similar, with no product named.

variables.desc: Which automated-driving feature(s) the coverage names. Naming a feature is not evidence it was in use.

variables.name: engagement_status
variables.label: Was the feature in use?

values.confirmed_by_official_source: A police or regulator finding, a court finding, or the manufacturer's own data report states the feature was in use.
values.claimed: Someone says it was in use (for example the driver, or police relaying the driver's account) and coverage reports no official confirmation.
values.alleged_in_legal_filing: The claim that it was in use is made in a lawsuit or criminal case.
values.under_investigation: Coverage says whether it was in use is unknown or being investigated.
values.disputed: Sources in the coverage contradict each other about whether it was in use.
values.reported_not_engaged: An official source or the manufacturer says it was not in use.
values.mentioned_only: The feature is mentioned as background; nobody in the coverage says it was in use.

variables.desc: The strongest statement the coverage supports about whether the feature was in use at the time. This records what coverage reports; it is not a finding by this dataset.

variables.name: engagement_claimed_by
variables.label: Who says it was in use
variables.desc: Everyone the coverage reports as saying the feature was in use.

variables.name: driver_seat_occupied
variables.label: Someone in the driver's seat

values.yes: A person was in the driver's seat.

variables.desc: Whether coverage says a person was in the driver's seat.

variables.name: driver_condition_mentioned
variables.label: Driver condition mentioned

values.alcohol_or_drugs: Alcohol or drug impairment is alleged or reported.
values.asleep_or_drowsy: The driver is said to have been asleep or drowsy.
values.distracted: Phone use or another distraction is reported.
values.not_supervising: Hands off the wheel, eyes off the road, or otherwise not monitoring.

variables.desc: Conditions of the person responsible for the vehicle that coverage mentions. Mentions, not findings.

variables.name: fatalities
variables.label: Deaths reported
variables.desc: Number of people coverage reports as killed. 0 only when coverage says nobody died.

variables.name: injuries
variables.label: Injuries reported
variables.desc: Number of people coverage reports as injured but not killed. 0 only when coverage says nobody was hurt.

variables.name: persons_harmed
variables.label: Who was harmed

values.subject_vehicle_driver: The driver of the vehicle in question.
values.emergency_or_road_worker: A police officer, firefighter, medic, tow operator or road worker.

variables.desc: Roles of the people reported killed or injured.

variables.name: police_action
variables.label: Police action

values.citation_issued: A citation or ticket was issued.

variables.desc: The furthest police action that coverage reports.

variables.name: criminal_charges
variables.label: Criminal charges
variables.desc: Charges reported, in a few words (for example "DUI; reckless driving"). No names.

variables.name: criminal_case_stage
variables.label: Criminal case stage
variables.desc: The furthest stage of any criminal case that coverage reports.

variables.name: civil_litigation
variables.label: Civil litigation
variables.desc: The furthest stage of any lawsuit about the incident that coverage reports.

variables.name: regulator_involved
variables.label: Regulator or safety board

values.nhtsa: U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
values.state_regulator: A U.S. state agency such as a DMV or utilities commission.
values.non_us_regulator: A regulator outside the United States.

variables.desc: Regulators or safety boards that coverage says are involved in this incident.

variables.name: responsibility_attributed_to
variables.label: Responsibility attributed to

values.driver: The person responsible for the vehicle.
values.automation_or_manufacturer: The automated-driving feature or its maker.
values.road_or_weather_conditions: Road design, work zones, weather or lighting.

variables.desc: Where anyone quoted or cited in coverage places responsibility. This records attributions made by others; the dataset never judges fault.

variables.name: coverage_stage
variables.label: Stage of coverage

values.follow_up_investigation: Later reporting on an investigation or new findings.
values.legal_proceeding: Reporting on charges, a lawsuit, a trial or a verdict.
values.retrospective: A look back at an older incident.

variables.desc: What the most recent coverage is mainly about.

claim_topics.automation_engaged: Says the feature was in use.
claim_topics.automation_not_engaged: Says the feature was not in use.
claim_topics.automation_performance: Describes what the feature did or failed to do.
claim_topics.driver_behavior: Describes what the person responsible for the vehicle did or their condition.
claim_topics.cause_or_responsibility: Says what caused the incident or who is responsible.
